One resource is settled once and spends one grant; a later obligation naming the same exact identity is reported as discharged by the canonical obligation and takes no second grant.  An obligation that cannot prove an exact identity is never treated as an alias of anything.
repaired_after_refusal.test_premise_corrected: The delegated mixed-drain test created an empty cgroup whose own close() discharged it before the drain began, so its assertion that the path still existed could not hold.  The obligation now carries a live member, so its removal genuinely is outstanding when the drain reaches it.  The failing assertion is unchanged and now passes for the right reason, and the state it exposed has its own deterministic and delegated coverage.
repaired_after_refusal.zero_grant_gate: _grant_or_observe makes the grant itself the gate: a grant carrying no time is no grant, nothing is settled, and no cleanup primitive runs.  Proved by a drain on an already-expired deadline leaving a removable cgroup physically present with zero calls to the destructive primitive.

repaired_after_second_refusal.fixture_preconditions_proved: The mixed-drain fixture now proves its own premise physically before asserting on it: the occupant is observed alive in /proc, and read_cgroup_members reports exactly that pid in the exact unregistered cgroup, immediately before the zero-grant drain.
repaired_after_second_refusal.outstanding_work_is_a_set: cleanup_evidence()['outstanding_work'] is a tuple of every obligation that is genuinely outstanding -- containment, processes, registration -- so two simultaneously outstanding obligations are both named.  cleanup_retry_operation remains a single next operation and keeps the accepted reap-before-release precedence unchanged.
repaired_after_second_refusal.regression: test_an_assertion_after_the_first_drain_still_leaves_no_residue builds exactly the shape that leaked -- a registered and an unregistered obligation, both populated, one bounded drain that settles nothing -- then raises, and proves the teardown leaves no cgroup, no live or zombie owned process, no registry entry, no reservation and no restoration debt.
repaired_after_second_refusal.teardown_survives_an_assertion: The delegated class registers _teardown_every_obligation as a cleanup, so it runs whether the body returned or raised, on a fresh independent budget, through the production drain.  guard_process_wide_unregistered_cleanups now discharges the obligations the test added before restoring the list instead of dropping them unremoved.
repaired_after_second_refusal.the_controller_reaps_its_own_children: The physical fixtures no longer waitpid an owned child behind the controller.  They kill nothing and reap nothing themselves; the production settlement kills the exact owned domain and positively reaps its own children, which is what makes cleanup_complete reachable.  The _reap_quietly safety nets remain registered for teardown only.

Exactness of the final removal rests on an explicitly bounded trusted computing base: one process-wide lock per delegated cgroup parent, which excludes every controller-owned mutation in this process and nothing outside it.  Linux offers no remove-by-handle primitive for a directory, so no atomicity is claimed against a process outside that boundary; outside it the removal refuses, retains the obligation and classifies the refusal.

The drain's global bound is an absolute deadline, not a real-time guarantee: a stage that over-sleeps returns late, so the observed wall clock may exceed the configured total by ordinary scheduler jitter.  No stage is ever granted time beyond the one deadline.

requirement_dispositions.note: The final destructive removal is bound to an explicit per-parent exclusion boundary and acts descriptor-relative to the retained parent, or refuses and retains; the whole cleanup drain spends one absolute budget across registered and unregistered obligations; registry capacity is granted only to a proved, linear, registry-issued reservation.
